body:
`MultiplayerPeer::disconnect_peer` is a virtual function, so the exact implementation could vary based on the peer implementation. 


[`SceneMultiplayer::get_peer_ids`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f92f1ce9c07d35b0e3843415bf99a509d3a51add/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp#L546) (which is exposed to the API as `get_peers`) consults it's own internal list of peer int ids, `connected_peers`

IDs are removed with [`_del_peer`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f92f1ce9c07d35b0e3843415bf99a509d3a51add/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp#L398). This is invoked in a few ways, but it is connected to the `peer_disconnected` signal when you set the peer using `Multiplayer.MultiplayerPeer =`. With forced resulting in no signal, I believe `_del_peer` is not being run as a result, leading to this issue.

The ENet implementation of [`disconnect_peer` ](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f92f1ce9c07d35b0e3843415bf99a509d3a51add/modules/enet/enet_multiplayer_peer.cpp#L278) when forced = true seems to directly erase the peer from it's list of peers, and from the `ENetConnection`'s list. I'm not certain on the _why_ of this preventing the signal from occurring (my read on the enet c code is inadequate), but it seems without that signal, the peer isn't being removed from `SceneMultiplayer`'s list.
